chemical peels are a safe, cost-effective and effective procedure that can be used to treat a range of skin conditions.

there is no single chemical peel that is best in all respects, and that the selection of the most appropriate peel for a particular patient should be based on the individual's skin type, the depth of the peel required, the area to be treated and the experience of the practitioner.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of chemical peels in Australia is widespread, and the majority of dermatologists use a combination of peeling agents.
chemical peeling can be a useful tool in the dermatologist's armamentarium, but it should be used in the context of an overall skin management program.
the most popular peel is the glycolic acid peel, followed by trichloroacetic acid peels and then the salicylic acid peel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lack of consensus among Australian dermatologists on the use of chemical peels.

chemical peels remain an important treatment option in dermatology, and that there has been a shift away from superficial peels and toward deeper peels, particularly the trichloroacetic acid peel, which is now the most popular type of peel used in Australia.
